100	endpoint used to be **silent and permanent**: a dispatch label nothing picked up, re-armed hourly,
101	repeating forever with no comment anywhere. Now the hand-off is a synchronous API call, so an
102	endpoint this repo has not configured — or one whose token secret is unset — converges the item to
103	`needs-human` naming what is missing, on the item itself. If promote or discover-packs has quietly

107	— lives with [the growth pack's extract-from-conversations skill](../../../../packs/claudinite-growth/skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md)
108	(applied by the conversation half of its growth-extract daily task over captured logs), and the
109	member-side method docs (extract, dedup, pack discovery, and how a project's local packs are
110	identified) live with [claudinite-growth](../../../../packs/claudinite-growth/README.md).

toolUseResult.prompt:
You're helping with a "lessons extraction" pass over recent GitHub activity in the repo missingbulb/Claudinite. Use the GitHub MCP tools (mcp__github__pull_request_read, etc — search for them via ToolSearch if not yet loaded, e.g. "select:mcp__github__pull_request_read") to read these 4 merged PRs FULLY: the diff, AND the review discussion (comments, review threads) — the review discussion is usually the richest source, since it records what was tried, what a reviewer pushed back on, and why the landed shape won.

PRs to read: #1357, #1355, #1352, #1350

Owner: missingbulb, repo: Claudinite.

Look for durable, reusable engineering/process lessons — things that would help a FUTURE agent session working on this repo avoid a mistake, work faster, or follow a convention it wouldn't otherwise know. This repo is "Claudinite" — a framework of packs/rules/checks that AI agent sessions follow when working on repos, so a lesson is typically about how automated agent work, code review, git/CI mechanics, or repo tooling should behave.

Bar to clear (most PRs will NOT yield anything — that's fine and expected):
- A review comment that names a convention the author missed
- A PR that went several rounds because its approach got re-decided mid-flight, and why
- A fix whose reasoning isn't obvious from the diff alone
- NOT a lesson: an already-settled, already-enforced implementation choice (a check/test already pins the shape) — that's just "why it looks like this"
- NOT a lesson: routine feature work with no friction or surprising correction

For each PR that yields a candidate lesson, report: PR number, one-line what happened, and the candidate lesson (1-2 sentences) with why it's non-obvious — quote the specific review comment or diff detail that grounds it. For PRs with nothing, just say "PR #N: nothing".

Keep the final report under 700 words total — tight, no padding.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.

You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. input.prompt:
You're helping with a "lessons extraction" pass over recent GitHub activity in the repo missingbulb/Claudinite. Use the GitHub MCP tools (mcp__github__pull_request_read, etc — search for them via ToolSearch if not yet loaded, e.g. "select:mcp__github__pull_request_read") to read these 4 merged PRs FULLY: the diff, AND the review discussion (comments, review threads) — the review discussion is usually the richest source, since it records what was tried, what a reviewer pushed back on, and why the landed shape won.

PRs to read: #1348, #1342, #1338, #1337

Owner: missingbulb, repo: Claudinite.

Look for durable, reusable engineering/process lessons — things that would help a FUTURE agent session working on this repo avoid a mistake, work faster, or follow a convention it wouldn't otherwise know. This repo is "Claudinite" — a framework of packs/rules/checks that AI agent sessions follow when working on repos, so a lesson is typically about how automated agent work, code review, git/CI mechanics, or repo tooling should behave.

Bar to clear (most PRs will NOT yield anything — that's fine and expected):
- A review comment that names a convention the author missed
- A PR that went several rounds because its approach got re-decided mid-flight, and why
- A fix whose reasoning isn't obvious from the diff alone
- NOT a lesson: an already-settled, already-enforced implementation choice (a check/test already pins the shape) — that's just "why it looks like this"
- NOT a lesson: routine feature work with no friction or surprising correction

For each PR that yields a candidate lesson, report: PR number, one-line what happened, and the candidate lesson (1-2 sentences) with why it's non-obvious — quote the specific review comment or diff detail that grounds it. For PRs with nothing, just say "PR #N: nothing".

Keep the final report under 700 words total — tight, no padding.

- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.

- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. - repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.

- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. {"number":1357,"title":"Import parseBlockedBy, and make the step it is in reachable from a test","body":"Refs #1354

**`main` on `main` is currently broken.** The first scheduler run after #1355 merged — [run 470](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32781936929) — died:

```
ReferenceError: parseBlockedBy is not defined
    at main (packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/scheduler-run.mjs:603:21)
```

`parseBlockedBy` has been used in `main` and never imported since the request lane was written. The line sits inside `for (const r of requests)`, and `requests` was always empty — so it never executed once across three days of green runs. #1355 made that list non-empty for the first time and the second bug surfaced immediately, hiding behind the first exactly as long as the first lasted.

I own this: #1355 is what put it in front of a runner.

## Why no test could reach it

Nothing drives `main` — its body is I/O against a live Action, so an identifier it names and never imports resolves at run time or not at all. There is no linter in this repo either, so an undefined name in an unexecuted path has nothing standing between it and production.

The blocker resolution is now an exported step, `blockersToResolve(items, requests, known)`, with both callers' rules unchanged — a blocked item's `Blocked-by` targets and a marked issue's, minus whatever `known` already answers. A test calls it, which is the whole of why the import can no longer go missing quietly. Verified see-it-fail: removing the import again turns those two tests red with the same `ReferenceError`.

## How it was caught

By forcing a scheduler run against the merged fix instead of waiting for the cron. That is the only reason this was three minutes of breakage rather than twelve hours.

## Verification

- Full suite **2742 pass, 0 fail**; `check_the_work` exit 0; `check_the_world` **0 blocking, 88 advisory** — unchanged.
- The 25 requests are still unadopted. The run that adopts them is the proof, and I'll force and watch it again once this lands.

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/   the missing import, and the blocker-resolution step lifted out of main so it can be called
packs/claudinite-tasks/         version 60824.9, with its VERSIONS row
```

{"number":1355,"title":"The request lane reads again: one listing per mark, and no failed read passing as an empty one","body":"Closes #1354

25 open issues wear `task:origin:ad-hoc` and have never been touched — every one still has `updated_at` equal to `created_at`. The scheduler has run 40+ times over them, each reporting success.

## What was wrong

`listMarkedIssues` asked GitHub for both marks in a single call:

```js
labels=${encodeURIComponent(`${ORIGIN_AD_HOC},${REQUEST_LABEL}`)}
```

under a comment asserting `The label filter is OR across a comma-separated list`. It is conjunctive — a comma-separated list selects issues carrying *every* name on it. So the query asked for issues wearing both `task:origin:ad-hoc` and the retired `claude-task`, which nothing has ever done. Empty list, nothing to adopt, green run.

60b1b65 (#1138) replaced the working single-label query with the pair at 2026-08-21T09:58Z. The oldest un-adopted mark, #1154, was filed at 10:02Z — four minutes later. Nothing has been adopted since.

Each mark is now its own listing, unioned by issue number so an issue wearing both spellings is adopted once and not twice.

## Why it survived three days of green runs

Two silences, and leaving either one would let this recur:

**No test touched the read.** `scheduler-run.test.mjs` covers the adoption *plan* with `requests` handed in directly, so nothing could disagree about whether that list is what GitHub would return. The new `marked-issues.test.mjs` covers the read, against a fake that models GitHub's **real** conjunctive filter — a fake that ORed would have agreed with the broken reader and proved nothing. Written first: all five assertions were red before the fix.

**A failed read was an empty read.** `if (status !== 200 || !Array.isArray(json) || json.length === 0) break;` collapses a 403, a 502 and "no requests" into one outcome. Even with the filter fixed, any transient failure reproduces this symptom exactly. Both listings now throw instead — a run that could not read is distinguishable from one that had nothing to do, and `report-failure` surfaces it.

The second commit carries that to `listWorkItems`, the structurally identical listing beside it, where the consequence is worse than a quiet no-op: breaking mid-pagination means the run plans against a truncated queue, so a standing item whose page never arrived reads as absent and the run mints a second one beside it.

## Verification

- Full suite: **2740 pass, 0 fail** (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`).
- `check_the_work` exit 0; `check_the_world` **0 blocking, 88 advisory** — unchanged from `main`.

The 25 waiting requests are not adopted by this PR. They are adopted by the first scheduler run after it merges, which is the real verification and which I'll watch.

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/    both issue listings; each mark asked for alone, and a failed read now fails the run
packs/claudinite-tasks/          version 60824.8, with its VERSIONS row
```

You're helping with a "lessons extraction" pass over recent GitHub activity in the repo missingbulb/Claudinite. Use the GitHub MCP tools (mcp__github__pull_request_read, etc — search for them via ToolSearch if not yet loaded, e.g. "select:mcp__github__pull_request_read") to read these 4 merged PRs FULLY: the diff, AND the review discussion (comments, review threads) — the review discussion is usually the richest source, since it records what was tried, what a reviewer pushed back on, and why the landed shape won.

PRs to read: #1335, #1302, #1315, #1314

Owner: missingbulb, repo: Claudinite.

Look for durable, reusable engineering/process lessons — things that would help a FUTURE agent session working on this repo avoid a mistake, work faster, or follow a convention it wouldn't otherwise know. This repo is "Claudinite" — a framework of packs/rules/checks that AI agent sessions follow when working on repos, so a lesson is typically about how automated agent work, code review, git/CI mechanics, or repo tooling should behave.

Bar to clear (most PRs will NOT yield anything — that's fine and expected):
- A review comment that names a convention the author missed
- A PR that went several rounds because its approach got re-decided mid-flight, and why
- A fix whose reasoning isn't obvious from the diff alone
- NOT a lesson: an already-settled, already-enforced implementation choice (a check/test already pins the shape) — that's just "why it looks like this"
- NOT a lesson: routine feature work with no friction or surprising correction

For each PR that yields a candidate lesson, report: PR number, one-line what happened, and the candidate lesson (1-2 sentences) with why it's non-obvious — quote the specific review comment or diff detail that grounds it. For PRs with nothing, just say "PR #N: nothing".

Keep the final report under 700 words total — tight, no padding.

4	
5	    Pass the whole secrets context to the executor in one static line (#1302)
6	    
7	    The executor workflow named every secret it passed, and the wiring converge
8	    regenerated that list from `required_secrets` plus configured endpoint tokens.
9	    That made the file a function of the task set — and `.github/workflows/` is the
10	    one path a converge cannot write, so every new secret needed a human-merged PR
11	    in every member. #1296 is what that cost: a member whose agent could only be
12	    started by a token its live workflow did not pass, and whose workflow could only
13	    be delivered by that agent.
14	    
15	    `toJSON(secrets)` is the one way Actions offers to pass all of them, so the step
16	    carries `CLAUDINITE_SECRETS: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}` and stops tracking
17	    declarations. secrets-bag.mjs is the only reader.
18	    
19	    The selection moves inward, which tightens rather than loosens it: code-work
20	    used to inherit the executor's whole environment and see every stamped secret,
21	    though only 6 of 22 code-work tasks declare one. It now gets exactly the names
22	    its own declaration lists, which is what DESIGN §14.4 always claimed.
23	    
24	    A member's live executor moves only by human-merged PR, so the reader falls back
25	    to the plain environment when no bag is present; a rehearsal fixture holds that
26	    shape. Retiring the fallback is gated on no member still stamping, not a date.
27	    
28	    Also fixes the endpoint-token message #1296 called out for asserting a cause the
29	    code cannot observe.
30	    
31	    Refs #1301, Refs #1296
32	    
33	    Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

{"number":1348,"title":"Stop the update precondition guessing whether the member is behind","body":"The question this task exists to ask — *is this member behind the canon?* — **cannot be asked from a scheduler run.** The Action deliberately does not read canon (DESIGN §3.3): `stamp.canonHead` is always null, and no signal carries the canon's versions.

That correction matters, because #1344's own "fix direction" said to compare the stamp against the canon's declared versions. It isn't implementable without reversing that design decision and putting a canon fetch in every member's hourly scheduler run. This PR takes the other route.

## What was wrong

Two proxies have stood in for the unavailable comparison, and both answered a different question:

- A **datetime in the declaration** recorded the last *full re-vendor*, so a member converging nightly read as months overdue forever (#1252).
- **Local movement in the window** — `convergedInWindow && !changedPacks.length` — reads as *"nothing happened here lately"*, which is equally true of a member that is current and one that canon moved past an hour after its own converge.

The second proxy is what stalled the fleet today. LaughCounter and TLDR sat four declared packs behind and missing a seeded one, each declining its own update at pick:

```
14:04:03  Claimed by executor actions-32736360596
14:04:06  The precondition declined: the mount converged in this window and no pack moved — nothing due
```

A forced wake could not override it — `wake:` readies the item, but the precondition is re-evaluated at pick, so the fleet lever mints work that converges to a no-op. Both members had to be converged from the canon side by hand.

## The change

The decline is gone. Only `!stamp.present` remains — a repo with no mount has nothing to update.

The asymmetry settles it, and it is not close: **declining wrongly costs permanent, silent staleness that nothing in the member can repair; running wrongly costs one converge that finds nothing and exits.** The precondition's own contract already says it "gates only that the worker RUNS; the worker owns every decision after that" — this stops it second-guessing the worker on a question it cannot see the inputs to.

Cost is one no-op converge per member per day, since the task is `frequency: 'daily'`.

## Verification

The test that asserted the decline now asserts the opposite, written first and watched fail. Full suite 2734 passing, `check_the_work` clean.

Closes #1344

{"number":1352,"title":"Delete the engine/scheduler shims, and repoint the worker off the updates/ ones","body":"L4, **split in two**. Supersedes #1329, which treated the two shim trees as one step. They have different retirement gates and cannot go together — and merging #1329 as written would have wedged all 13 members on their next update run.

## `engine/scheduler/` — gone

Safe now: nothing in the canon imports it (only tests reference it), and it is named by member **workflow** files, which all 13 now point at the pack mount.

With it go the vendor set's two temporary rules — the engine walk that shipped the shims only where the pack shipped, and the tolerance that shipped `claudinite-tasks` whether or not a member declared it (every stamp carries it now). The reviewed barrier exception that let `engine/scheduler/` name a pack goes too, and `scheduler-workflow-shape` stops accepting the engine path as a scheduler entry.

## `updates/` — kept, one more cycle

**This is the half #1329 got wrong.** The worker resolves its flows against a *fresh canon clone at HEAD*, not its own mount:

```js
git(['clone', '--depth', '1', CANON_URL, tmp]);
const load = async (rel) => import(pathToFileURL(join(tmp, rel)).href);
const { engineUpdate } = await load('updates/engine-update.mjs');
```

So the surface a member calls is whatever **its** vendored worker names — and every member vendored a worker naming `updates/*` earlier today. Deleting the tree fails every member's next update at module resolution, unrepairable, because the repair *is* the update. #1329 deletes it without repointing those calls, despite its body claiming otherwise.

This repoints the worker at `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/*`, so the next converge fields a worker that no longer needs the shim. The tree comes out in a follow-up, gated on reading the members' vendored workers — never a date.

`install.test.mjs` now pins **both** surfaces, because both are fielded. #1329 rewrote it to pin only the new one, which would have switched off the single test guarding this.

## The 21 dangling references, resolved by kind

Deleting `engine/scheduler/` makes 21 references dangle. They are not all the same thing:

| Count | What they are | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | Fixture **member workflows** in `vendoring/rehearsal/` | Repointed to the pack, exactly as the real fleet was today |
| 8 | **Legacy wire literals** | Moved to one shared module beside a single waiver |
| 2 | Incidental fixture paths | Repointed |
| 1 | A past-incident narrative in a comment | Trimmed so it reads without spelling a path |

The eight are the interesting ones. A work item minted before the move still carries `engine/scheduler/` in its machine block, and `BUILT_IN_PATH_RE` accepts that root **permanently** — its own comment says why: it is a validator, so dropping either root rejects that half of the ad-hoc request lane outright. Those literals are protocol a decoder must keep understanding, not pointers to files that must exist. `reference-integrity` cannot tell the difference, so they now live in `packs/claudinite-tasks/test/legacy-protocol.mjs` with one accept entry against it — rather than five waivers scattered across the tests that exercise the decode, which is also the shared-constant rule applied to a literal that was copied five times.

The `tick.mjs` entry alternation is deliberately **left alone**: that is #974's migration, with its own gate and its own test file. Retiring two unrelated tolerances in one PR is how a gate gets missed.

## Verification

Full suite 2734 passing, `check_the_work` clean, `check_the_world` 0 blocking. The advisory count drops 142 → 88 — the `file-placement` advisories the shim files were carrying.

```
engine/scheduler/            deleted
packs/claudinite-lifecycle/  the worker names the flows' real home; the cron check drops the engine entry path
packs/claudinite-tasks/      legacy wire literals get one home
packs/claudinite-canary-repo/ a README link followed the move
vendoring/                   the shim gating and the undeclared-pack tolerance come out; fixture workflows repointed
.claudinite-settings.json    the engine/scheduler barrier exception out, one reference-integrity waiver in
```

Refs #1328

{"number":1342,"title":"Count what the scheduler run readied in its own drain gate","body":"The drain gate asks GitHub what is in the queue as the scheduler run's last act. That read is eventually consistent, so it can miss an item the same run created milliseconds earlier — and the run then reports an empty queue, skips the drain, and leaves the item it just minted sitting `task:ready` until the next cron fire.

This is not theoretical. It is what stalled the fleet delivery this afternoon, on three members at once:

| Member | Item | Created | Gate's verdict | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [LaughCounter#304](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/issues/304) | `claudinite-lifecycle/update` | 13:10:52.017 | `nothing pickable` | 377 ms |
| [ClaudiniteCanary#253](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/253) | `claudinite-lifecycle/update` | 13:10:42.598 | `nothing pickable` | 584 ms |

Each was a **forced** `update` — so the delivery the force existed to make never ran, and the members stayed short of the `claudinite-tasks` mount while their schedulers ran green every hour. A run that succeeds while silently dropping its own work is the worst shape this can take: nothing is red, and the tracker reads as converged.

## What changed

The verdict is now the union of two sources rather than one read:

- what `listOpenWorkItems` returns, ordered by `pickOrder` as before;
- what **this run itself readied** — created-as-ready, readied out of blocked, reclaimed to ready, or woken by `CLAUDINITE_WAKE`.

The run does not need a read to confirm what it just wrote. `pickableCount` is exported so the seam is testable directly rather than only through the workflow's text shape.

The gate's purpose survives intact: a run that readied nothing over an empty queue still dispatches nothing, so a quiet repo still costs zero executor invocations. Ordering stays the executor's job — this only decides whether to start one, and it errs toward starting.

No sleep, no retry, no re-read.

## Delivery

`engine/scheduler/queue/scheduler-run.mjs` re-exports this module, and members still `run:` that legacy path, so this reaches every member through the ordinary nightly converge with no member-side workflow change.

Closes #1340

{"number":1350,"title":"Retire the twice-daily-cron migration tolerances","body":"Supersedes #1234, which cannot be rebased: it was written before the task surface moved into `packs/claudinite-tasks` (#1317), so it edits `engine/scheduler/calendar.mjs` — now a shim — and bumps `claudinite-lifecycle` for a change that lives in `claudinite-tasks`. Re-authored on `main` with both halves intact.

**Both gates are met, each read off the fleet rather than a date.**

## The cron tolerance

`scheduler-workflow-shape` stops accepting the hourly line. Its gate was every member's workflow PR having landed. All 13 now carry the two-tick form:

```
ClaudiniteWebsite 26 4,16   CrosswordChat 21 4,16   EdFringeNow 49 4,16
GoogleCalendarEventCreator 24 4,16   LaughCounter 49 4,16   MissingBulbWebsite 39 4,16
Shepherd 11 4,16   ShoutsAndWhispers 48 4,16   TLDR 45 4,16
VascularColoring 11 4,16   WIP 34 4,16   hitbut 46 4,16
```

plus ClaudiniteCanary. `missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite` was the last holdout on `39 * * * *` and moved in missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite#230.

## The frequency tolerance

`LEGACY_FREQUENCIES` is **emptied, not deleted** — the map *is* the tolerance, so emptying it collapses `ACCEPTED_FREQUENCIES` onto `FREQUENCIES`, makes a declaration still naming a retired token fail contract validation, and leaves `normalizeFrequency` as the identity every caller keeps calling. Nothing is unwired, and the next retirement refills it.

Its gate was no member's own declarations naming a retired token. A sweep of every member's local packs found exactly one — `GoogleCalendarEventCreator`'s `create-extractor` — which moved to `daily` in missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator#1061. Worth noting it had *already* been running daily: the door normalized it away, so the declaration was promising a cadence the queue had stopped honouring.

## What the tests say now

The tests that existed to prove each tolerance are **inverted rather than deleted**, so the corpus still states what the door does: a retired spelling fails validation, and the calendar refuses it instead of inventing an anchor. Scenario S70 is rewritten around the shut door rather than dropped.

One deliberate non-change: `periodMs` still answers a day for an unrecognized token. Its *fallthrough* — not the door — is what keeps one off an hour-scale bound, which is what would park a task `needs-human` on every janitor sweep. That safety outlives the vocabulary it was written for, and its own comment predicted exactly this.

The simulator's mirrored copy of the map is emptied with it, so the sim keeps modelling what the engine writes rather than the rule's old intent.

Two rehearsal fixtures carried the retired cron incidentally while modelling old *structural* shapes (the `tick.mjs` entry, the ungated drain); their crons move to the two-tick form. `custom-anchor-hour` gets `9,21` from its own `dailyHour` rather than the default — both hours being a function of that value is precisely what it exists to prove, and a fixture on `4,16` would pass the shape check while contradicting itself.

## Verification

Full suite 2734 passing, `check_the_work` clean, `check_the_world` 0 blocking.

```

packs/claudinite-lifecycle/  the cron check stops accepting the hourly line; version 60824.5
packs/claudinite-dashboard/  a fixture's stock frequency was a retired token
vendoring/rehearsal/         two fixture crons, and custom-anchor-hour's own anchor hours
```

Closes #1233

{"number":1335,"title":"Ship the tasks pack in the engine lane while the legacy shims name it","body":"The live canary caught this on #1326's merge commit, and nothing in the suite could have.

Closes #1334

## What broke

The engine and pack lanes deliver on separate cycles. The `engine/scheduler/` shims are engine-lane files that re-export a pack, so a member converging its engine first held a shim pointing at a pack its mount did not carry yet — the old dashboard version it still had imports `engine/scheduler/queue/work-item.mjs` by name, the shim resolved to nothing, the pack failed to load, and the self-test gate refused to land the converge. Which also meant the member could not receive the pack that would have fixed it.

## The fix

A shim and its target are one unit, so the lane that ships one ships the other: `isEngineFile` carries `packs/claudinite-tasks/` for as long as the shims exist. It comes out with them in [#1329](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1329).

## The test that was missing

It asserts the invariant rather than this instance: **every import in the engine lane must resolve inside the engine lane.** Neither existing guard could see the defect — the fielded-import scan asks whether a path resolves in the canon, which it did, and the rehearsal fixtures are all built from the current canon, so none of them holds the older pack version that makes the window visible. Seen to fail without the fix.

## Verified against the real canary, not a fixture

Cloned `missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary` and ran the actual flows:

- `engineUpdate` → `ok`, converged tree passes its self-test (it failed here before the fix)
- `packUpdate` → `ok`, and the declaration now carries `claudinite-tasks`, seeded by the migration record
- the member's own vendored `check_the_world` → exit 0
- the exact `run:` line its workflow carries — `node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/scheduler-run.mjs` — executes **as the program** through the shim and prints its run report, which is the L2-window risk closed

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. - artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

Retiring the fallback is gated on no member still stamping — a converge-confirmable condition, not a date. ## Known cost, recorded rather than rediscovered Every repo secret reaches the executor **job**'s env (no task subprocess sees more than it declared). And masking is registered per exact literal, so a secret containing `"`, `\` or a newline appears JSON-escaped in the bag and would not be masked if something printed it — theoretical for token-shaped values, but real, and now stated in DESIGN §14. {"number":1337,"title":"Name the executor's secrets again; `toJSON(secrets)` is what GitHub flags","body":"Reverses #1301's one-line secret bag, on the owner's call.

## What was wrong

`CLAUDINITE_SECRETS: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}` is the shape GitHub's malicious-workflow detection flags. A flagged workflow does not run until a person clicks **Approve**, and it parks with **zero jobs** — from the queue's side that is indistinguishable from "nothing was pickable". An unattended fleet can neither absorb that nor notice it. It started two minutes after #1302 merged (fd4cb68 at 08:31:14 UTC; first park 08:33:31 UTC) and had been silently eating executor runs in the canon and in Shepherd ever since — it is why L1's fleet-baseline saw 8 of 13 members fail to reach canon.

## What this does

- The executor workflow lists each secret by name again, and the wiring converge — now the tasks pack's `converge-workflows.mjs` — regenerates that list at the `# claudinite:secrets` marker from every declared task's `required_secrets` plus the configured endpoint tokens.
- **The cost this reinstates is not pretended away**: the file becomes a function of the task set, `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot write, and a NEW secret therefore needs a human-merged PR in every member — the coupling that wedged one in #1296. The owner took that trade explicitly: a rare human-merged PR beats a permanent human click on every run.
- `queue/secrets-bag.mjs` **stays**. Its selection — a task's code-work sees exactly the names its own declaration lists, rather than inheriting the executor's whole environment — was #1301's other half, is independent of how the secrets arrive, and keeps working off the plain environment. Its bag *reader* stays too, because every member carries the bag-setting workflow until its own PR lands; retiring it is gated on no member still stamping a bag, a converge-confirmable condition, never a date.
- Both windows now have a rehearsal fixture: `stamping-executor` for the named shape, and a new `bag-executor` for members sitting inside this reversal's own window.
- A stub guard pins `toJSON(secrets)` out of both stubs — seen to fail with the line put back.
- The design docs that stated #1301's decision now state this one, with what it costs.

## Folders touched

```
.github/workflows/     executor workflow names its secrets again, at the marker
docs/                  tasks-dispatch and task-code-work DESIGNs restate the decision
engine/                converge-wiring hands the workflow half its config
packs/claudinite-tasks/  converge-workflows regenerates the secret list; secrets-bag
                         keeps selection + a transitional bag reader; stub + tests
vendoring/             rehearsal fixtures gain bag-executor
```

## Verification

`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` → exit 0, 0 failures. `check_the_work` → 0 blocking. `check_the_world` → 0 blocking.

Closes #1336

{"number":1315,"title":"Cut the local pack's RULES.md to one trigger and directive per rule","body":"Closes #1312

`.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/RULES.md` carried 63% of this repo's session rule tokens (~11,500 of ~18,300) and had grown ~900 tokens a day over the preceding week.

**8,435 → 5,359 words (37%), 114 → 154 rules.** Session rule tokens ~18,300 → ~14,000.

Two passes, one commit each.

## Pass 1 — the audit method

The `authoring-agent-docs` audit that #760 and #894 ran on `packs/basics/RULES.md`. That one worked by folding clauses back into parent rules; this file barely had that problem, since `growth-extract` already appends one situation-keyed block per lesson. What it had was **per-rule incident archaeology** — issue ids, dates, quoted owner exchanges, the story behind each rule. Removed, per the skill's own line: *"the commit that added the rule keeps them… a rule that reads as a post-mortem with a directive at the top is the wrong way round."*

Three structural changes, each verified against the tree first:

- **Split out** *Creating the artifact a check will demand* — a trailing clause of the mechanize-a-procedure rule, but a reader can arrive at it without that one.
- **Cut** *Writing check-the-work* — `basics` already carries see-it-fail as the ladder rule, and both load in the same session.
- **Cut** *Judging whether a member is fresh* — it **contradicted** `claudinite-lifecycle`, which loads beside it: the local rule said read `ref`, the canon rule rules out `ref` along with `claudinite.updated`, because the versioned flows stamp versions only. Whichever a session reached first decided the answer.
- **Stripped** *Diagnosing a member's maintenance PR that won't land* to the one diagnosis `claudinite-lifecycle` does not already carry verbatim.

## Pass 2 — one trigger, one directive

67 words/rule was still too long, because most rules carried their reasoning inline and several carried two or three situations in one block. A bundled rule cannot be trimmed without losing one of its situations, so this pass splits first, then cuts.

**113 → 154 rules, mean 35 words, median 35, longest 53.** Reasoning is out; measurements survive only where the number *is* the argument (the 81% wall-clock, the 25-of-26 minutes, the 46 truncated test files).

Representative splits: *Landing a change to what members receive* separated from *Forcing fleet delivery* (the second fires once you have already decided to); *Changing an export in `updates/*`* from its retirement condition; the scheduler-workflow rule from where to move the program.

The header now carries the budget, so appends hold the shape:

> Keep each rule near 40 words: the trigger, the directive, and a consequence clause only where the rule cannot be applied without it. Split a rule that carries two situations; the evidence it came from lives in `VERSIONS.md` and the issue, never here.

## Verification

A subject diff is meaningless across a 113 → 154 split, so coverage was checked two ways:

- **Identifiers** — every backticked identifier the old file named, matched against the new one. Twenty missing: sixteen were examples that re-expressed their rule (`ensure_ascii`, `build_vars`, `git stash`); four were load-bearing and restored — the literal `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/collaborators/{u}/permission`, `converge-item.mjs`, `engine/checks/helpers/session-transcript.mjs`, `pack-discovery-entry-await`.
- **Subjects** — every old rule subject matched to a new rule by shared content words. None unmatched.

`check_the_work` clean. `check_the_world` **0 blocking**, 77 advisory (unchanged), none against this pack. Full suite **2,708/2,708**. No line over 100 bytes, clearing the seven that tripped the advisory `rules-line-length`.

## Carried out separately

The `packs/* → .claudinite/local` barrier gap, which was sitting as a TODO inside a rule, is now #1313 with its four still-dangling `canon-curation` references listed.

The header budget binds sessions that read this file. Holding `growth-extract` itself to it is a change to the two extract skills in the canon — a separate PR, not done here.

{"number":1359,"title":"Pin that packUpdate already sweeps an absorbed pack's leftover mount directory","body":"Refs #1188

## What #1188 asked for

A member's converge should remove `.claudinite/shared/packs//` for
each absorbed pack (`chrome-extension-release`, `github-actions`,
`firebase-release`), via a new migration-record delete op — reasoning that the
pack flow "replaces a declared pack's tree wholesale but never removes a tree
that has stopped being declared."

## What I found

That reasoning is true of the *general* pack flow, but the absorption case
already has its own mechanism: `legacySpellingsOf` in
`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/pack-update.mjs` (added alongside the
original collapse in #1081) sweeps every `RENAMED_PACKS` legacy spelling —
renames and absorptions alike, since the map represents both shapes the same
way — whenever a pack update lays down its survivor's directory. It was
written for exactly this problem and, per its own test coverage, was only ever
pinned for the pure-rename shape (`core` → `claudinite-lifecycle`), not for an
absorption where the leftover sits *beside* its survivor rather than alone.

I confirmed this empirically against real members rather than only a fixture,
the same way #1186 was confirmed: I cloned all seven repos #1186 found frozen
(CrosswordChat, GoogleCalendarEventCreator, TLDR, EdFringeNow, LaughCounter,
ClaudiniteWebsite, MissingBulbWebsite). Every one converged today
(2026-08-24) once #1187 unfroze the fleet, and none carries a leftover
absorbed-pack directory or a legacy spelling in its declaration or stamped
`packVersions` anymore. The existing sweep already did the job as soon as a
converge could land.

## What this PR does

No production code change — the composed rules already produce the right
answer, so adding a new migration-record delete op would be redundant
machinery duplicating what already works. Per this repo's own rule for this
exact situation ("if they do [produce the right answer], add no production
code: pin it with a regression test that asserts the contrast case too"), I
added one test to `engine-tests/pack-update.test.mjs`, mirroring the existing
rename test but for a real absorption (`chrome-extension-release` →
`chrome-extension`): it plants the leftover directory, runs `packUpdate`, and
asserts both that the leftover is swept *and* that the converged tree
self-tests clean (the contrast case — #1186's actual failure mode). I verified
the test is not vacuous by temporarily disabling the sweep and watching it
fail, then restored the source.

## Not in this change

The issue also flagged, as a secondary "worth checking" item, whether the
absorbed ids can now come out of `RENAMED_PACKS` (its retirement rule: no
member's declaration or stamped `packVersions` still carries the old
spelling). The seven members above are clean, but I don't have a canonical
fleet-wide member list to check exhaustively, so I left the map untouched
rather than guess at full-fleet coverage.

## Folders touched

**`engine-tests/`** — one new regression test; no other file changed.

---

Since this item carries no `Merge:` field, I'm not merging this myself — it's parked for review.

{"number":1314,"title":"Fleet dashboard: read the fleet horizontally, one pass at a time","body":"The fleet sweep read one member end to end — repo, head, declaration, tree, issues, runs, usage fold, pack cards, commit graph — before starting the next. Four at a time, but still depth-first per member, so the viewer's rate limit was spent in the wrong order: the first members got their decoration before the last members were looked at at all, and a ceiling hit mid-sweep turned the tail of the roster into `withheld` rows underneath tiles reporting that nothing was on fire.

The sweep is now horizontal. Every member goes through one pass before any member starts the next, cheapest and most load-bearing first:

| Pass | Reads | Buys |
|---|---|---|
| identity | repo, head, declaration | what the repo is, and whether it runs Claudinite — the only calls a non-member ever costs |
| attention | one issues page, one runs page | every fault a row can report: the lead card, the tiles, the ranking |
| depth | tree, the member's usage fold | declared tasks, and the month behind each row's figures |
| packs | each declared pack's descriptor and values | the member's own cards, and `latest-release` where a pack asks |
| activity | a year of commit activity | the row's graph, and nothing else |

A budget that runs out now costs the same panel on **every** row rather than the last members entirely — a fleet missing its graphs still answers "where do I need to look"; a fleet missing its tail does not.

Two things fall out of the split. A member is summarised only once its attention pass lands, never at identity: `summariseMember` reads an unread queue as an empty one, and a row saying "nothing parked" about a member whose issues have not been fetched is a wrong statement rather than a partial one. And the progress line names the pass while the passes behind the ranking are still filling columns in, since a counter reaching the roster's length five times over otherwise reads as the page starting again.

The ordering lives in `fleet-sweep.mjs`, pure and testable: passes, `appliesTo` populations, per-member error containment, the concurrency cap. `view-fleet.mjs` keeps only what each pass fetches.

- Full suite: 2711/2712 (the one failure is `engine-pack-lane-shims`' shallow-clone guard, which this sandbox's clone trips regardless of the change). `check_the_work` clean, `check_the_world` 0 blocking.

{"number":1345,"title":"Promote-to-canon: lessons from MissingBulbWebsite, Shepherd, VascularColoring, WIP","body":"Refs #1308 — growth-promote run over target members MissingBulbWebsite, Shepherd, VascularColoring, WIP.

All items land as **prose** (no rung-3 check candidate was confidently authorable — every item is judgment/behavioral, or the pattern spans arbitrary scripts and project-specific paths).

| Pack | Origin | Landed rule |
|---|---|---|
| `basics` | Shepherd | Check whether an `AskUserQuestion`'s answer is already decided before asking; batch several open decisions into one question. |
| `basics` | MissingBulbWebsite | Never publish a public claim about a real, named person from a secondary/data-broker source when the primary source is blocked — ask instead. |
| `git-github` (`git-github-advanced`) | MissingBulbWebsite | `codeload.github.com` can be blocked by a sandbox's egress proxy where ordinary `git clone` isn't — use `git clone --depth 1` instead of a tarball fetch. |
| `git-github` (`git-github-advanced`) | WIP | Resolve a wait on a GitHub Actions run/check through exactly one mechanism (the `Monitor` tool, or direct polling) — never a background sleep alongside a separate blocking poll. |
| `basics` (`writing-tests` skill) | WIP | Sharpened the existing see-it-fail restore guidance: restoring a **staged** destructive test mutation needs `git checkout HEAD -- `, not a bare `git checkout -- ` (which restores from the index and leaves the staged mutation in place). |
| `basics` (`repo-text-sweeps` skill) | WIP | Patch a hand-maintained JSON config as anchored text, never a `json.load`/`json.dumps` round-trip (reorders keys, changes indent, re-escapes strings with nothing failing). |
| `claudinite-growth` (`unattended-agents` skill) | Shepherd + WIP | Don't duplicate work already delegated to a background subagent — wait for and read its output first. (Two of this run's four target repos independently reported this.) |
| `claudinite-growth` (`unattended-agents` skill) | Shepherd | Don't manufacture a no-op tool call while waiting on a background subagent with nothing to do — state the wait in plain text instead. |
| `claudinite-growth` (`extract-from-conversations` skill) | WIP | A captured `conversation-logs` JSONL line can be large enough to overflow a raw `Read`'s token cap even at a small offset/limit — check line lengths first. |
| `flutter` | WIP | Real file/image I/O inside `testWidgets` must run inside `tester.runAsync`, or the fake-async test zone never completes it and the case hangs. |
| `research-project` | VascularColoring | Sharpened the ground-truth rule: never validate against the pipeline's own prior output, which validates nothing. |

## Notable rejections (already covered)

- **GitHub MCP list/search token-overflow (`fields`/`minimal_output` over `per_page`)** — independently reported by MissingBulbWebsite and WIP, but already fully covered by `git-github-advanced`'s "Cap *and* qualify every list/search call" section (fields subset, small page size, read the spilled overflow file).
- **Shallow-clone `origin/main` staleness** — reported by Shepherd, already covered by `git-github-advanced`'s "The sandbox checkout can be shallow" section (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` + `--unshallow`, generalized to "any cross-branch history comparison").

- MissingBulbWebsite's `site-copy` "lead with actual behavior" item — a duplicate of the existing `basics` privacy-claims rule.
- VascularColoring's other items (self-validation circularity aside) are already substantially covered by the `research-project` pack, which this repo's own local pack largely originated from.
- Several Shepherd/WIP items (Claude Code Web PR-diff rendering, a Claudinite-queue `converge-item.mjs` Action-only limitation, external-docs JSON-mirror fetch tips) were judged too narrow, too uncertain, or without a clean existing/new home, and were left for a future pass rather than forced into a home that doesn't fit.

{"number":1237,"title":"Chain 3/3: retire the twice-daily-cron migration tolerances","body":"Link 3 of #1225's execution chain — the last one, and the **delayed task that merges #1234**. Everything you need is here.

```
Blocked-by: #1236
Retry-every: 7 days
Model: sonnet
```

## What this removes

#1234 is written, reviewed, rebased onto `main` and mergeable. It empties `LEGACY_FREQUENCIES`, so `hourly` / `daily-2h` / `daily-1h` / `daily+1h` stop being accepted in a task declaration, and it stops `scheduler-workflow-shape` accepting the legacy hourly cron.

**It must not be merged early, and the reason is measurable.** `scheduler-workflow-shape` is severity `blocking`; on #1234's branch it emits a finding for an hourly cron; and a member's converge **withholds** `.github/workflows/` — the one path it cannot push — so a member holding the old cron cannot fix itself. Merging before every member's workflow PR has landed turns the whole fleet red on a file none of them can repair.

## What makes this step's world ready

#1236 closed, **and** the precondition below reads true. Converge-confirmable, never a date — if it does not hold yet, this is a wait, not a failure.

**No member's own task declarations still name a retired frequency.** Canon packs are already migrated; what matters is each member's `.claudinite/local/packs/*/tasks/*/task.mjs`, which is member-authored and which no vendoring pass rewrites. Grep each member for `frequency: 'hourly'`, `'daily-2h'`, `'daily-1h'`, `'daily+1h'`.

Retiring early does not merely fail such a task. `periodMs` also feeds the janitor's stale-ready bound and the precondition's signal window, so an un-normalized token makes a daily task judged against a bound it was never sized for — a `needs-human` park on every sweep.

## The playbook

1. Check the precondition across every member. If any still declares a retired token: comment which member and which file on #1225, push `Not-before` forward by `Retry-every`, clear this issue's `task:status:*` label, and leave it open. No other comment — the bumped field is the record. Fixing that member's declaration is the way to unblock this, and is worth doing.
2. Precondition holds → fetch #1234's branch and confirm it is still current against `main`; rebase if `main` has moved under it.
3. Run the full suite: `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`, and `check_the_work`.
4. Green → merge #1234 (squash).

**Already done, 2026-08-22 — do not redo:** the branch was rebased onto `main` after #1230 merged, and the `pack-version-bumped` false green called out in #1234's body is resolved — `claudinite-lifecycle` is `60822.3` against main's `60822.2`, and `check_the_work` is clean against the true base. Step 2 is a re-check, not the original rebase.

Note the two tolerances have **different** gates. The cron half's gate — every member's workflow PR landed — is satisfied by #1235. If the frequency half is still blocked long after, split the commit and merge the cron half alone.

## What counts as this step having worked

#1234 merged, suite green, and no member red on its next converge.

## How it ends

Comment on #1225 that the tolerances are retired and the migration is complete, then close this issue as completed. #1225 can close with it.

{"number":1236,"title":"Chain 2/3: verify the twice-daily cron in production — 2 scheduler runs a day, not 24","body":"Link 2 of #1225's execution chain. Everything you need is here.

```
Blocked-by: #1235
Not-before: 2026-08-25T06:00:00Z
Retry-every: 1 day
Model: sonnet
```

## What this proves

The whole point of the change: the scheduler was **71% of private Actions spend** at ~26 min/day per member, because Actions bills each job rounded up and the cron fired 24 times a day to do about 13 minutes of work. Two ticks a day should make that ~2 min/day. Nothing so far has measured a real repo — only the simulator.

## What makes this step's world ready

#1235 closed (every member on the new cron), **and** at least one full UTC day has elapsed since, so there is a complete day to count.

## What to observe

For each **private** member — the ones that cost anything; public repos are free and unlimited:

1. **The count.** Scheduler workflow runs for one complete UTC day. Expect exactly **2**. Baseline: 24.
2. **Nothing was dropped.** No task's standing item is missing its occurrence for that day — a cheaper cron that quietly stopped instantiating work is a regression, not a saving.
3. **The risk the simulator could not model.** A whole day's chain now settles serially inside one executor run. Read the longest executor run's duration against the workflow's `timeout-minutes: 350`. The simulator's task durations are fixtures, so this is the first real read of whether a member's day actually fits.

## What counts as this step having worked

Every private member shows 2 scheduler runs for the measured day, no missing occurrences, and no executor run near its timeout.

## When the check fails

Comment what you read and **leave this issue open** — closing releases the next link.

- Still 24 runs on some member → its workflow never landed; reopen #1235's question there rather than proceeding.
- Missing occurrences → this is a real regression in the cadence change. Reopen #1225 with what is missing and stop the chain.
- An executor run near the timeout → do **not** fail the step, but say so plainly on #1225: it is the residual risk the plan named, and it wants its own issue rather than silence.

## How it ends

Comment the per-member figures on #1225 — runs/day before and after, and the longest executor run — then close this issue as completed. That close releases Link 3.

{"number":1291,"title":"Verify in production: the drain job actually runs drain-dispatch.mjs","body":"#1290 moved the scheduler workflow's drain from an inline `github-script` block to `node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/drain-dispatch.mjs`. Unit tests cover the module, and the thin workflow itself has been watched running green on `missingbulb/Shepherd` ([run 32638669087](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/actions/runs/32638669087)) — but on that run the queue was empty, so the `drain` job was **skipped by its own gate** and the new module has never actually executed inside a member's Actions job.

That is the one path worth proving live. It runs on every tick that leaves work pickable, and its failure mode is silent: the workflow parses, the run goes green, node exits on a bad path or a refused dispatch, and the queue simply stops draining. No test can answer whether the vendored path resolves and the job's token can fire the dispatch from inside a member repo — only a real run can.

{"number":1169,"title":"Dissolve docs/skill-usage-metrics/DESIGN.md into the packs that own its subjects","body":"The owner's read, and it holds up against the tree: this design doc collapses into the pack that collects the signals and into the dashboard. It is 769 lines describing a pipeline that is now built, and the canon's own rule for that is already written — *behaviour belongs in the module header and the pack README*, not in a doc that has to be kept in step with both.

The evidence, section by section (line counts from `2026-08-21`):

| § | Lines | Where it already lives, or should |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Where knowledge lives | 16 | A standing architectural rule ("the canon knows mechanisms, never repos") — belongs with the local pack's standing decisions, not in one initiative's doc |
| 2 Sources of truth | 18 | `claudinite-growth/README.md` |
| 3 Capture (3.1–3.5) | ~100 | `claudinite-growth/README.md` already carries the capture lifecycle and retention almost verbatim; `capture-log.mjs`'s header carries the rest. **§3.4 (capturing an unattended session, where no SessionEnd hook fires) and §3.5 (the ordering constraint) are the one part with no other home** — they go into the pack README beside the lifecycle they belong to |
| 4.1 Check activations | 101 | Duplicated: `usage-fold/README.md`'s "The check failures are the win" and `fold-usage.mjs`'s header both carry the three marks, the CI-in-the-loop rule and the floor property |
| 4.2 Task invocations | 69 | Describes the retired slot-scheduler census. Keep two sentences of it as history in `usage-fold/README.md` (which already has them) and drop the rest |
| 4.3 Exec statuses | 16 | `usage-fold/README.md` |
| 5 The per-repo aggregate + shape | 146 | Duplicated: `usage-fold/README.md` and `usage-format.mjs`'s header |
| 6 The fleet aggregate | 63 | Superseded; **deleted outright** — the task it describes goes in #1166 |
| 7 Consumers | 40 | Split: the promotion-ladder half to `claudinite-growth/README.md`, the reader half to `claudinite-dashboard/README.md` |
| 8 TTLs | 12 | `claudinite-growth/README.md` (it already states retention) |
| 9 Failure modes | 45 | Duplicated: `usage-fold/README.md`'s "Failure is visible, never silent" |
| 10 + the two later rounds | 57 | Owner decisions with their rationale. These are the doc's only irreplaceable content — move them to the local pack's standing decisions, where a session actually reads them |

So the shape of the change: **almost nothing is written fresh.** Two sections move (§3.4/§3.5, and the decision record), one is deleted, and the rest is verified as already-covered and then dropped. If a section turns out *not* to be covered where this table claims, write it into the pack — do not keep the doc alive for it.

## The references are the real work

Eight files point into this doc by section number, and a dangling `§` pointer is worse than no pointer:

```
engine/hooks/session-end-command.mjs          §3.3
engine/scheduler/run-record.mjs               §4.2
packs/claudinite-growth/session-end.mjs       (unnumbered)
packs/claudinite-growth/tasks/usage-fold/task.mjs        §5
packs/claudinite-growth/tasks/usage-fold/worker.mjs      §5
packs/claudinite-growth/tasks/usage-fold/fold-usage.mjs  §4, §5
docs/per-project-scheduling/DESIGN.md         §4.2 and one unnumbered
```

Each becomes either a pointer to the pack README section that absorbed it, or — better where the sentence was only citing itself — nothing at all. Use the `repo-text-sweeps` skill; grep for `skill-usage-metrics` afterwards and confirm zero hits outside history.

## Done looks like

`docs/skill-usage-metrics/` is gone; no file in the tree references it; the owner decision record is in the local pack's standing decisions; §3.4 and §3.5's content is in `claudinite-growth/README.md`; the full suite and `check_the_world` are green.

## Worth deciding while doing it

The same argument applies to the other five `docs/*/DESIGN.md` — `tasks-dispatch` alone is 1,958 lines and is cited from dozens of module headers. **Do not sweep them in this change.** If the pattern holds, say so in a comment here and let the owner decide separately; a 4,300-line doc migration is not something to discover mid-run.

#1287 removed the `node:fs`/`node:path` import that reached the dashboard's browser module graph through `engine/settings-file.mjs`, which was leaving the published page a blank screen (#1286). The page loads clean from a local checkout, and the new `browser-graph.test.mjs` pins the property in CI — but neither watches the **published** site.

Production here is another repo: the dashboard is served from GitHub Pages by the member that declares `claudinite-dashboard` (`https://missingbulb.github.io//`, Shepherd at the time of filing). The canon's bytes reach it only after that member's nightly converge re-vendors `engine/` and the pack, and after its own Pages workflow deploys. Neither had happened when this was filed, and neither can be forced from the canon.

One thing to watch while verifying: a converge push is authored with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which fires no `on: push` workflow (#1094). A converged mount with a stale deployed site is a real possible outcome, and it is a failure to report, not a wait to extend.
